# Spiritual Translation of the Chapter Concerning Three End owments of the Celest ial Human

---

** ¶2:** Three essential spiritual endowments, each distinct from the others, were made manifest in the most ancient celest ial will — the first and in most church of hum ankind. By virtue of these end owments, this celestial will was found to surpass and exceed all other spiritual faculties joined together , whether belonging to interior states or to exterior states .

**¶3:** The first endowment: The very lik eness of the Divine itself was impressed upon the celestial will. The natural aff ections and hereditary incl inations that formed the external mind received their pattern from the radiant form of Divine Good and Truth , which had been displayed to them from the interior. By virtue of this, the form of the Divine within the celestial human exceeded in beauty every other spiritual faculty , whether of the interior mind or of the exterior.

** ¶4:** The second endowment : The celest ial will was in wardly constit uted through the prim ordial wisdom proceeding directly from the Divine — the first born of all interior and exterior states — together with the five fundamental faculties of spiritual perception. By virtue of this, the interior structure of the celestial human was found to differ from the structure of all other forms of spiritual life, since the form of each kind of life is pecul iar to itself. But in the celestial human, the interior life corresponds perfectly to the just distribution of the fundamental goods and truths in their proper order. Therefore the celestial human poss esses a perception of spiritual re alities that surpasses every other form of life and every natural aff ection.

**¶5:** The third endowment: All interior truths, all counsel s of wisdom, and the impress of every spiritual faculty — both of the interior mind and of the exterior — were gathered together by the form ative aff ections and sealed within the celestial will . The celest ial will and its companion understanding became a dwelling- place and a hab itation for all kn owledges of good and truth in their spiritual order, and for all states and changes of spiritual life — the greater cycles and the lesser cycles and the full courses of regener ation. For the form of the entire spiritual universe is contained within the celestial human, as in a living image . By virtue of this, all interior states and all exterior states were set into motion on his account; dist urbance and conflict arose because of him between those aff ections that are of the Divine and those that are of self . The divine affections drew him toward eternal life, because their own lik eness and form had been placed upon him; while the self-derived affections were drawing him toward spiritual death, so that through him they might se ize dominion and establish their own rule , and through him bring the whole spiritual order into subjection.

** ¶6:** Furthermore , understand that the self -derived affections and natural incl inations determined the form of the celestial will so that they might exercise dominion through him and establish their rule , and they did this according to seven purposes , which are as follows.

**¶7:** The first purpose : The celestial will became the source of illumin ation within their domain — a substitute for the wisdom that had rad iated from the Divine Human when it appeared to them from within . For all the natural affections desired to possess the likeness of the Divine Human for themselves. Their will was drawn after it with lon ging.

**¶8:** The second purpose: So that through the celestial will they might seize wisdom and contain it, and obst ruct the asc ent of truth back toward its Divine source.

**¶9:** The third purpose: So that by means of the Divine likeness impressed upon the celest ial will, all that is of the Divine — both in interior states and in exterior states — might be brought into subjection; on account of the appearance of that spl endor, that beauty, that sur passing excellence . For the celestial will sur passes in its out ward form every other created thing .

**¶10:** The fourth purpose: The celestial will is a determining form and a living template , so that every subsequent state of spiritual life that would be begotten might be brought forth according to the same pattern.

**¶11:** The fifth purpose: That through the celestial will all the operations and capac ities of every spiritual faculty — interior and exterior, hidden and manifest — might be displayed ; and that through him the whole of spiritual reality might be ordered , and every truth be made apparent within him.

**¶12:** The sixth purpose: That a great protection might exist for the self -derived affections by virtue of the Divine likeness placed upon the celestial will; for i nasmuch as the interior powers would recognize their own image even within what had fallen under the domin ion of natural incl inations, no judgment or destruction would be brought against those incl inations on account of the celestial will that bore the Divine form .

**¶13:** The seventh purpose: That the celestial will might become the ruling principle, the sovereign , and the master over all aff ections and perceptions; and that through him the self -derived nature might establish complete dominion over the whole of spiritual life .

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Three great things that are distinct were revealed in Adam the first human. Indeed, due to this, he was found to be better and more outstanding than the conjoined powers that are in heaven and on earth.

The first: The image of the exalted one was placed upon him. The creators and moulders of his body sealed him after the shining form of the image that had been displayed to them above. Indeed, due to this, the image of Adam was found to be surpassingly beautiful beyond any conjoined power above and below.

The second thing: Adam was shaped in his structure through the light of the first-born of heaven and [earth, and through the elements of] the five sons. Indeed, due to this, his structure was found to differ from the structure of even the other creations; [sin]ce the form of all creations is different. As for Adam, the formation of his soul fits over the correct distribution of the elements. Therefore, he has intelligence surpassing that of the other creations and beasts.

The third are the teachings and counsels and the seal of all the powers above and below. The creators, who set him in order, gathered them and sealed them in him. Adam and his consort Eve became a dwelling and home for the signs of the zodiac and the stars; and the months, the days and the years. For the seal of the entire universe is stamped upon Adam. Indeed, due to this, heaven and earth moved because of him; trouble and disorder arose on his account between they that are good and they that are evil. So, the good induce him to life because of their image and shape placed upon him; while the [wi]cked were drawing him to death, so that they would have power through him and they would conceive the kingdom, and through him humiliate the entire universe.
Furthermore, understand that the rulers determined and formed Adam so that they would be masters through him and conceive the kingdom because of seven things.

The first: He became the enlightener in their creation; instead of the light of the image of the Ambassador who had displayed himself to them above. For they all desired the likeness of the image of the Ambassador. Their heart was drawn after it.
The second: So that they would scoop up the light through him and restrain and obstruct it from its ascent to the heights.

The third: So that because of the image of the Ambassador that is placed upon him the entirety of the divine that is above and below would be humiliated; on account of the likeness of the splendour, of the beauty of his superiority. For he is superior in his appearance to all creatures.
The fourth: He is a seal-ring and a new impression, so that all births who will be begotten might be brought forth after his seal.

The fifth: That might be displayed through him all the skil[ls] of the powers, they above and below, secret and manifest; and that they might determine through him the totality, and every thing be revealed in him.

The sixth: That there would come to be a great protection for them through the image of the exalted one that was placed upon him; for as the heavenly would [behold their own image upon him, they would not bring destruction upon] even rulers; and no evil thing would be done to them on account of Adam.
The seventh: That he might become chief and king and master over all creatures; and they might conceive the kingdom through him.
